analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/gemma-decode-keeps-spaces.md, lines 1-5) and a paragraph added to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1584-1592). No executable code is supplied. The LocalTokenizerLoader.swift change the docs describe is not in this batch, so I could not check the implementation.

The documented behavior resolves an absent `clean_up_tokenization_spaces` to false in memory and keeps an explicit Boolean. It changes only the text decoded from the same tokens. Token IDs, sampling, model state and cache keys are stated to be unchanged. If that holds, the prefix-cache threat T-041 is not affected: cacheSalt, HMAC lookup tags and the AAD are untouched, and no new at-rest artifact appears. No authorization, attestation, encryption, or billing boundary is touched.

One behavioral note is not a vulnerability. Stop-string matching now operates on spelled text, so stops matching only the cleaned text no longer fire. This could slightly change output truncation, but I see no confidentiality or integrity consequence.

The next review pass should confirm in the code that the config is rewritten only in memory, not written back to the model directory. It should also confirm that the fix does not alter the tokenizer inputs used for cache keys, and that the prompt-render path (input IDs) is independent of the decode setting. The doc claims all three, but the supplied evidence does not verify them. These are unverified contracts, not findings.
